result.title: Measurement Artifacts in Trustworthiness Evaluations of Quantized Small Language Models
result.summary: Evaluations of quantized language models attribute the change in a benchmark score to quantization. We write the measured change as the true change plus a term contributed by the instrument. Instrument error that is the same at every precision can shrink a paired comparison but cannot create or reverse an effect. Error that interacts with quantization can do both, and it is reported as an effect of quantization. We estimate this interaction for four measurement choices in 8 instruction-tuned models below two billion parameters, at float16, LLM.int8() and NF4, on identical items. Measured against labels from two human annotators, the 4-bit rise in harmful compliance is about half to two-thirds of the rise in non-refusal that a corrected key word detector records. Cloze and lettered multiple-choice scoring disagree about the effect of quantization far more than their noise allows: their estimates correlate at \r{ho} = 0.10, against a ceiling of about 0.77. LLM.int8() answers and generations depend on which items share a batch, and padding alone changes its answers. Rounding activations to 8 bits is enough to produce this dependence. NF4 is batch-invariant. The two largest reported calibration losses are response-bias shifts. We release item-level predictions, option scores and human annotations, and give recommendations for evaluating compressed small models.

AI.brief_summary: 论文把量化模型基准分数的变化拆成真实变化与测量工具贡献的误差项，在8个小于2B的指令微调模型、float16/LLM.int8()/NF4三种精度上估计评分方式、批内共享项、padding与校准损失四类测量选择与量化的交互效应，并发布条目级预测与人工标注。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「工具误差与处理效应交互、评分格式可反转结论」的分析框架可能可供核查 LVR 诊断中把增益归因于 latent 推理而非评分/批处理伪影的问题，但研究对象是纯文本量化模型，与视觉状态无直接联系。
